name: Other-emptiness (gzhan stong)

definitions.definition: The ultimate — buddha-nature, dharmakāya, dharmatā — is empty of all adventitious conventional phenomena, which are other than it, and not empty of its own nature and qualities; it is permanent and not a dependent arising.
In Kongtrul, the Great Madhyamaka view suited to meditative experience; in Mipham, acceptable in the sense that unconditioned wisdom is empty of the adventitious while not established by own-nature.

relations.note: the two readings of how the ultimate is empty — not yet reconciled
the Jonang take RGV 1.154-155 literally as the doctrine of other-emptiness

notes: Other-emptiness is also held, each in his own form, by Shākya Chokden (Sakya; tch:shakya-chokden), the 8th Situ (tch:situ-panchen) and Jamgön Kongtrul (Rimé); only the Jonang and Rimé definitions are given here.

name: Self-emptiness (rang stong)

definitions.definition: Emptiness of own-nature; the Jonang accept it of every conventional phenomenon and deny it of the ultimate.
In Kongtrul's tenet presentation, the Madhyamaka of Nāgārjuna's reasonings, valid for cutting elaborations.

relations.note: the self-emptiness of the rangtong Madhyamaka is the Madhyamaka's absence of own-nature applied to all phenomena

name: The Great Madhyamaka (dbu ma chen po)

definitions.definition: The definitive Madhyamaka of the third wheel, the Maitreya texts, Nāgārjuna's hymns and the Kālacakra, beyond the extremes because conventional phenomena do not truly exist and the ultimate does not not exist.
Kongtrul's summit of the sūtra tenets: other-emptiness Madhyamaka.

notes: The Nyingma (Rongzom, Mipham) use 'Great Madhyamaka' for a Madhyamaka of the union of appearance and emptiness; that usage is not merged here.

name: The two truths

names.name: bden pa gnyis (rang stong / gzhan stong)

definitions.definition: Conventional truth is empty of its own nature; ultimate truth is empty of other and not of itself. The two are not one entity, yet not different entities: they are different in the sense that their sameness is negated.

name: Buddha-nature (tathāgatagarbha, buddhadhātu)

definitions.definition: Buddha-nature is the ultimate itself, permanent, present in all beings complete with the buddha-qualities, empty only of adventitious stains.
Kongtrul reads it as the other-empty ground of the Great Madhyamaka; Mipham as the union of luminosity and emptiness, neither mere absence nor permanent entity.

name: The permanence of the dharmakāya

definitions.definition: Taken literally: the dharmakāya is permanent, stable, peaceful and eternal, not merely 'permanent' as an unbroken continuum.

name: The garbha empty and not empty

definitions.definition: The locus classicus of other-emptiness: the element is empty of separable stains and not empty of inseparable qualities — read as definitive.

name: The three natures (trisvabhāva)

definitions.definition: The imputational and the other-powered natures are conventional and self-empty; the thoroughly established nature is the ultimate, self-aware wisdom, empty of the other two (other-empty).

name: The three turnings of the dharma-wheel

definitions.definition: The third turning (with the Kālacakra) is definitive, teaching the other-empty ultimate; the second teaches the self-emptiness of the conventional.

name: The two ālayas: ālaya-consciousness and ālaya-wisdom

definitions.definition: The basis of all is twofold: the ālaya-consciousness (kun gzhi rnam shes), conventional ground of imprints, and the ālaya-wisdom (kun gzhi ye shes), the ultimate buddha-nature.

relations.note: the Laṅkāvatāra calls the tathāgatagarbha 'ālayavijñāna'; the Jonang reserve buddha-nature for the ālaya-wisdom
the Yogācāra store-consciousness is only the conventional ālaya for the Jonang

name: The emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects

names.name: rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong nyid

definitions.definition: The Kālacakra's ultimate — empty form united with unchanging bliss — identified by Dolpopa with the other-empty dharmatā, as opposed to an emptiness of annihilation.

relations.note: Dolpopa's identification of the tantra's and the sūtras' ultimate
unchanging bliss is the bliss aspect of the same ultimate
relations.standpoint: Kālacakra as read by the Jonang

name: The four ages of the doctrine (Dolpopa)

definitions.definition: The doctrine declines through the four ages; the definitive teaching of the age of perfection (kṛtayuga) is restored by Dolpopa's 'fourth council'.

name: The three bodhisattva commentaries (sems 'grel skor gsum)

definitions.definition: Three Indian commentaries held to be by tenth-level bodhisattvas — the Vimalaprabhā on the Kālacakra, Vajragarbha's commentary on the Hevajra, and Vajrapāṇi's commentary on the Cakrasaṃvara — which read the tantras in the definitive sense and are central authorities for the Jonang.

name: The ten signs of the Kālacakra

definitions.definition: The empty forms that appear in the branch of withdrawal of the Jonang six-branch yoga: smoke, mirage, fireflies, lamp, blaze, moon, sun, darkness, lightning and drop.

name: Chöd: cutting ego-clinging at the root

definitions.definition: What Chöd cuts is not an external enemy but self-clinging, the root of the mind's afflictions and of the four māras; the view of emptiness is applied as the blade.

name: The four guests of the Chöd offering

definitions.definition: The recipients of the visualized body-offering: the Three Jewels (devotion), the protectors (qualities), the six classes of beings (compassion), and harmful spirits and karmic creditors (repaying debts).

name: The Chöd feasts (distributions)

definitions.definition: The body-offering is visualized in several 'feasts' — white, red, multicoloured and black — differing in what the body becomes and to whom it is given (summary only; restricted).

notes: Membership and meanings recalled with low confidence.

name: Gods and demons as the mind's own display

definitions.definition: Gods and demons have no existence apart from the mind; as long as there is ego-clinging there are demons, and when it is cut there are none; hope of gods and fear of demons are both cut.

name: The lineages of Chöd

definitions.definition: Chöd is traced in a 'father' strand from Padampa Sangye and a 'mother' strand from Machig Labdrön, and distinguished as sūtra-tradition and tantra-tradition Chöd (and their union).

name: Chöd as the Dharma that went from Tibet to India (the tradition's account)

definitions.definition: Indian scholars tested Machig, accepted her teaching and carried it to India; the only Dharma said to have travelled in that direction.

name: Fearsome places (gnyan sa) and charnel grounds

definitions.definition: Places inhabited by powerful spirits — charnel grounds, lonely springs, trees and passes — where Chöd is practised because fear arises there and exposes self-clinging.

name: The instruments of Chöd

definitions.definition: The large hand-drum, the bell and the thighbone trumpet accompany the sung Chöd liturgy; the melodies are transmitted with the practice.

name: Pacification of suffering (zhi byed)

definitions.definition: Suffering is pacified by the realization of the Perfection of Wisdom — the 'mantra that pacifies all suffering' — combined with instructions of sūtra and mantra given according to capacity.

name: The three transmissions of Pacification

definitions.definition: Padampa Sangye's teaching was passed on in early, middle and later transmissions, the later through Dampa Kunga.

name: The three nyepa (rlung, mkhris pa, bad kan)

definitions.definition: Three principles that sustain the body in balance and cause disease when disturbed; they arise from desire, hatred and delusion and dwell chiefly in the lower, middle and upper body.

relations.note: the same three doṣas in physiology; the Tibetan system derives them from the three poisons

name: The fifteen subdivisions of the nyepa

definitions.definition: Each nyepa has five kinds with their own seats and functions.

name: The seven bodily constituents (lus zungs bdun)

definitions.definition: Nutritive essence, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow and regenerative fluid, each refined from the one before.

name: The three excretions (dri ma gsum)

definitions.definition: Faeces, urine and sweat, which with the nyepa and constituents make up the body's basis.

name: The mental origin of disease: ignorance and the three poisons

definitions.definition: The distant cause of all disease is ignorance of selflessness, never parted from beings as a shadow from a bird; from it come desire, hatred and delusion, and from them rlung, mkhris pa and bad kan.

name: The tree of healing (the three trees of the Root Tantra)

definitions.definition: The whole science summarized as three trees — the basis, diagnosis, treatment — with roots, nine trunks, forty-seven branches and two hundred and twenty-four leaves; flowers of health and long life; fruits of Dharma, wealth and happiness.

members: root of the basis (health and disease)

name: The three methods of diagnosis

definitions.definition: Looking (tongue, urine), touching (pulse) and questioning.

name: Pulse diagnosis in Sowa Rigpa

definitions.definition: Reading the radial pulse of both wrists with three fingers, each position linked to organs; constitutional, seasonal, disease and death pulses and the seven 'wondrous' pulses.

relations.note: parallel diagnostic method in later Āyurveda; historical relation not established here

name: Urine diagnosis in Sowa Rigpa

definitions.definition: Examination of urine in three phases for colour, vapour, odour, bubbles, sediment and film, and the reading of spirit influences.

name: The four methods of treatment

definitions.definition: Diet, behaviour, medicine and external therapy, from gentle to strong.

name: The six tastes in Sowa Rigpa

definitions.definition: Sweet, sour, salty, bitter, hot and astringent, each from a pair of elements, each pacifying or aggravating particular nyepa.

relations.note: same six tastes; the element-pair assigned to bitter differs (Tibetan water+wind)

name: The eight potencies and seventeen qualities

definitions.definition: Heavy, oily, cool, blunt, light, rough, hot and sharp potencies, with seventeen qualities of disorders and remedies and three post-digestive tastes.

name: The five elements in Sowa Rigpa

definitions.definition: Earth, water, fire, wind and space compose body, nyepa, food and medicine; tastes and potencies arise from them.

name: The seven constitutions (rang bzhin bdun)

definitions.definition: rlung, mkhris pa, bad kan, the three pairs and the combined type, each with its body and temperament.

name: Embryology in the Four Tantras

definitions.definition: Seed, blood and karma-driven consciousness with the five elements form the embryo, which passes through fish, tortoise and pig phases and is born after thirty-eight weeks.

relations.note: both teach conception from seed, blood and a transmigrating consciousness; stages differ

name: The four kinds of channels

definitions.definition: Channels of formation, of existence, of connection and of life.

name: Signs of death in Sowa Rigpa

definitions.definition: Distant, near and uncertain signs by which the physician judges curability.

relations.note: medical and yogic omens of death overlap

name: The eight branches of Āyurveda

definitions.definition: In the Four Tantras: body, children, women, spirits, wounds, poisons, old age and virility.

name: The Medicine Buddha's teaching in Tanaduk

definitions.definition: The Four Tantras are taught in the medicine city Tanaduk by the Medicine Buddha's emanation Rigpé Yeshe, at the request of Yilé Kyé, before four retinues.

name: The qualities of the physician

definitions.definition: Intelligence, altruistic intention (the four immeasurables towards patients), commitment, skill, diligence and knowledge of worldly conduct.

members: skill in body, speech and mind

name: Processed mercury (btso thal) and the precious pills

definitions.definition: Mercury, deemed poisonous, is detoxified and processed into an ash that becomes the base of the precious pills; the process is restricted to qualified masters. Restricted: no procedure recorded.

name: Rlung as the mount of the mind

definitions.definition: Rlung carries the mind as a horse its rider; disturbances of rlung show as mental agitation, and mental disorders are treated largely as rlung disorders.

name: Hot and cold disorders

definitions.definition: All disorders are finally hot or cold; mkhris pa and blood disorders are hot, rlung and bad kan cold.

name: Rejuvenation (rasāyana)

definitions.definition: Rejuvenation (bcud len) is the seventh branch, taught in the closing chapters of the Oral Instruction Tantra, with virility.

name: The Rimé (non-sectarian) approach

definitions.definition: Every authentic lineage is to be respected, received, practised and preserved in its own terms without mixing; disparaging another tradition is abandoning the Dharma; rare transmissions are to be collected and printed.

name: The eight great chariots of practice lineages

names.name: sgrub brgyud shing rta chen po brgyad

definitions.definition: Tibetan practice mapped as eight complete lineages of practice.

members: Orgyen Nyendrub (approach and accomplishment of the three vajras)

name: Jamgön Kongtrul's Five Treasuries

definitions.definition: The five great collections that preserve the Tibetan traditions.

members: Treasury of Knowledge (shes bya kun khyab mdzod)
Treasury of Kagyu Mantra (bka' brgyud sngags mdzod)
Treasury of Precious Treasures (rin chen gter mdzod)
Treasury of Extensive Teachings (rgya chen bka' mdzod)
notes: Some lists add or substitute the Uncommon Treasury (thun mong ma yin pa'i mdzod).

name: The seven transmissions (bka' babs bdun) of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo

definitions.definition: The seven modes by which Khyentse Wangpo held the teachings.
